school: Hinsdale Central High School, Hinsdale IL
method: v2 (the v1 swatches came out grey: two of the three 'brick' patches were on the shaded north front, where the sky fills the shadow and a tan brick measures R/B ~1.0). Swatches are now median LINEAR RGB of SUNLIT wall patches only (tools/textures/refs.py swatch), each white-balanced on a neutral in the same frame (sunlit concrete walk / steps), every patch cropped and looked at before it was used. Sunlit brick, entrance east return, commons_724aeb1734.jpg: [0.468, 0.347, 0.242] against concrete [0.799, 0.791, 0.730] (phone HDR, flattened: R/B 1.8). Entrance front, page_2b7f70cec7.jpg (architectural photo): [0.227, 0.130, 0.093] against the concrete steps [0.195, 0.191, 0.227] -> white-balanced hue R:G:B 1 : 0.58 : 0.35 (R/B 2.85). The courtyard photo page_d464c8d1af.jpg shows red-brown spandrel brick on the older wing. A student of the school confirmed the walls read red-brown, not grey. Face targets below take the hue between the two measurements, weighted to the architectural photo (R/B 2.9-3.6), at an albedo of 0.14-0.23 (G). Mortar is measured separately and no longer folded into the brick mean: the 1950 wing's joints are a weathered grey-brown, darker than the units; the additions' are lighter. Course height from the storefront door (2.13 m leaf) in commons_724aeb1734.jpg: 7.2 mm / px, courses ~9.4 px = 68 mm (modular brick, 3 courses = 203 mm).
